title: Three Ways to Get Big Flavor with Less Meat: Dan Dan Mien, Braised Collards, Anchovy-Powered Pasta
summary: This ATK segment demonstrates how to extract deep flavor from a small amount of meat across three dishes. It starts with a Dan Dan Mien where ground pork is browned in a thin smear for maximum surface contact, then builds a concentrated chili-oil-based sauce with Sichuan aromatics and a dried-yacai accent. A second showcase braises ham hocks to create a lush pot liquor for braised collard greens, emphasizing long, gentle extraction of flavor and collagen. The third demonstrates a fast, high-umami pasta sauce built around anchovies, plus a parsley-basil pesto that doubles as an umami booster, finished with pasta water to emulsify and lightly coat angel hair. Throughout, the host highlights techniques for flavorful results from limited meat, including browning, tension between texture and flavor, layering of aromatics, and science-backed umami boosters.

sections.description: Introduces a Dan Dan Mien approach that uses a small amount of ground pork browned in a thin smear on the pan, then minced or jabbed into tiny pieces so it browns evenly and clings to noodles. The sequence emphasizes maximizing surface area for faster cooking, rendering fat for roasty flavor, and building a porky base with aromatics before boiling noodles, blanching greens, and making the chili oil-based sauce.

sections.description: Presents Erica Turner's braised collard greens as a model of flavor extraction from a small meat component. The method centers on creating a flavorful pot liquor by simmering ham hocks with aromatics, then adding collards and cooking long enough to soften cell walls and concentrate the porky, smoky flavors into the greens. The section also covers prep steps for greens and final meat removal and recombination.

sections.description: Demonstrates a fast, intensely flavored pasta sauce built around four anchovy filets and a bright herb pesto. The segment explains the umami boost from inosinate in fresh anchovies together with glutamates from curing, and shows how to blend the sauce and then finish with starchy pasta water to create a clingy, creamy coating for angel hair noodles. The plating emphasizes sauce-first layering and finishing with greens and herbs.
